title: Component spec sheet (draft)
description: Draft model of a per-component spec sheet generated by `design-data spec-sheet`: pages of blocks, one block per relationship context, plus one generated block per relationship property for records that carry no context. Renderers draw each block's scene and add no layout of their own.

visual.description: True when the component has a visual recipe. False marks a table-only sheet: blocks carry token rows but no render, and views show "No visual recipe yet". The same stub is the starting point for a new component.

datasetRevision.description: Dataset revision (git commit) the sheet and its changelog were generated from.

size.description: Size key every block visual renders at.

title.description: The relationship context string the block documents, or, when titleSource is "property", the relationship property written as words.

titleSource.description: "context": titled by an authored relationship context. "property": generated for records without a context, one block per relationship property; views mark these so they read differently from authored groups. A generated block has an unmarked render (no highlight, markers or measurements) and no changes.

records.description: Relationship records the block's rows show.

render.description: The block's visual. Null on a table-only sheet (visual is false).

changes.description: Ids of changelog entries whose relationship context equals the title.

badges.description: Badges to show, for example "Values updated".

view.description: Fit of the scene into the block visual: scene px to block px scale, and the offset of the scene's origin in the block.

request.description: The render request the scene was solved from.

scene.description: The resolved scene graph (`design-data render --format scene`).

svg.description: The scene drawn as SVG (`scene_to_svg`, as `design-data render`). Written only with `design-data spec-sheet --svg`; views fall back to drawing nothing when it is absent.

highlight.description: Recipe part and prop pairs bound to the block's relationship context.

markers.description: Numbered markers 1..n, one per group of token rows that share a recipe property template. `part` is the recipe part the marker sits on, or null when no recipe binding fits. `drawn` is false when the visual has no node for the marker (no part, or the recipe does not draw it); its number stays on the rows and views note it as not drawn.

label.description: The group's relationship property with its size part dropped (the recipe's `{sizeIndex}`/`{size}` template without the placeholder). Distinct within a block.

derived.description: True when the group is a context the recipe derives from the layout (`derived` in the recipe) instead of binding.

measurements.description: Scene measurements the block shows on the Layout page: those whose relationship context is the block title (kinds `height`, `width`, `padding`, `gap`, `radius`, `border`, `focus-thickness`, `focus-gap`, `press`). A block renders in the states and options its bindings need (a focus ring in `keyboard-focus`, a pressed scale in `down`). `index` points into scene.measurements and `label` is the bound token's name, the same name the token rows show (the relationship property only when no token resolves).

derived.description: True for a context the recipe derives from the layout. The span is appended to scene.measurements (kind `padding`, token `derived from height`), and `label` is `derived from height` instead of a token name.

conditions.description: Scalar component options the relationship records pin for this row.

source.description: "token": the record references a token with $ref. "inline": the record carries its own value and no token; token.uuid is null and token.name is the record's legacy key or property.

label.description: Option label from component options or the registry.

marker.description: Number of the render marker this token belongs to, matching render.markers[].n.

values.description: Token value per scale (`desktop`, `mobile`) or color scheme (`light`, `dark`, `wireframe`), or `value` when the token has neither. An alias shows as {"alias": name}.
